papers.title: $L^p$-Liouville properties and realizations of Schr\"odinger operators on incomplete Riemannian manifolds
papers.abstract: The aim of the paper is to highlight and standardize in a self-contained framework the connections between some properties associated with the Laplace-Beltrami operator on possibly incomplete Riemannian manifolds. We present both new and well-known characterizations of the positivity-preserving property, essential self-adjointness, and Liouville-type results for $L^2$-functions, using the latter to establish a clear hierarchy among these properties. Furthermore, we prove the stability of the essential self-adjointness of the Laplace-Beltrami operator on incomplete Riemannian manifolds under the removal of closed (possibly non-compact) subsets from a complete manifold, subject to suitable conditions on their (generalized) Hausdorff measure. With appropriate modifications, this framework is adapted throughout the paper to the general $L^p$-case for $p\in (1,+\infty)$.

papers.title: Monotonicity and evolution of total isoperimetric profiles under Minkowski regularization
papers.abstract: We study the evolution of the total isoperimetric profile of a planar convex body under volume-preserving Minkowski regularization. Several scalar geometric quantities are known to be monotone along this flow; we prove that the total isoperimetric profile is monotone as well, and characterize the equality cases. We also establish an explicit reparametrization law, by which, for nonnegative times, the profile of the regularized body is determined by that of the initial one, and the order of profiles of bodies of equal area is preserved. As consequences, we obtain the uniform convergence of the profile to the one of the ball of equal area; its joint \(\mathrm C^1\) regularity in the volume and the regularization parameter; the fact that it solves a nonlocal quasilinear Hamilton--Jacobi equation; and sharp inequalities for the profile.

papers.title: Free boundary minimal hypersurfaces of Morse index one in Eucildean half-space
papers.abstract: We prove that a complete, connected, two-sided, embedded free boundary minimal hypersurface of finite total curvature and Morse index one in a half-space of RN, with nonempty boundary is a higher-dimensional half-catenoid. We also prove that a complete, connected, two-sided, embedded free boundary minimal hypersurface of finite total curvature and Morse index one in a quarter-space is the higher-dimensional quarter-catenoid.

papers.title: Ramification and Finiteness of Equivariant Minimal Surfaces
papers.abstract: Let $S$ be a closed oriented surface of genus $g$, with $g\ \geq \ 2$, and let $\mathcal X_0^{\mathrm{good}}$ be the good locus of $\operatorname{PU}(2,\,1)$ representations with Toledo invariant zero. For $1\ \leq \ b\ \leq\ 2g-3$, we show that representations admitting an equivariant minimal map of total ramification at least $b$, for some marked complex structure, form a countable union of compact null sets of Hausdorff dimension at most $16g-16-2b$. For larger $b$, this locus is empty. Consequently, on a dense $G_\delta$ subset of full measure in $\mathcal X_0^{\mathrm{good}}$, every nonconstant equivariant minimal map is an immersion, for every marked complex structure. On the convex cocompact locus, a dense $G_\delta$ subset of full measure consists of representations admitting a finite nonempty set of marked equivariant minimal immersions.

papers.title: Finite-Shift Inverse-Concavity and Exterior Noncollapsing for Fully Nonlinear Curvature Flows of Nonconvex Hypersurfaces
papers.abstract: We give a finite negative-shift criterion for preserving a prescribed exterior noncollapsing bound under fully nonlinear curvature flows whose hypersurfaces need not be convex. The criterion uses the optimized two-point expression of Andrews and Langford. We verify it by a uniform global two-matrix estimate for the explicit speed \[ F_{\varepsilon}(A)= tr A- \varepsilon\frac{\norm{A^{\circ}}^{2}}{ tr A} \] on the open cone \[ \Gamma=\{A\in\Sym(n): tr A>0, \norm{A^{\circ}}< tr A\}.\] Here $A^\circ$ denotes the trace-free part of $A$. This cone contains the positive cone and also matrices with a negative eigenvalue, while the displayed speed is concave and non-convex. For an explicit range of parameters depending on the initial exterior bound, the cone and that bound are preserved throughout the smooth embedded existence interval. Together with the known interior estimate for concave speeds, this gives two-sided tangent-ball bounds for this nonlinear family, including closed nonconvex initial hypersurfaces.

papers.title: A variational construction for Einstein metrics on connected sums of $S^2\times S^2$
papers.abstract: For each positive integer $n$, we give a variational construction of a positive Einstein metric on the connected sum of $n$ copies of $S^2\times S^2$, with coupled toric and dihedral symmetries. More precisely, we obtain these metrics via a min-max construction for the total scalar curvature, which is in some sense dual to the usual max-min formulation of the smooth Yamabe invariant within this symmetry class, with more favorable analytic properties.

papers.title: Spherical Milnor Spaces II: Projective Quotients and Higher Topological Structures
papers.abstract: We study projective and semidirect quotients of the spherical Milnor construction and develop a step-by-step lifting obstruction from their explicit spherical local sections. The resulting transition functions produce a twisted Cech 2-cocycle for any specified compatible extension with abelian kernel. When the kernel is $U(1)$ and the sign acts by complex conjugation, taking logarithms yields a twisted Dixmier--Douady obstruction under stated sheaf hypotheses. We identify its projective-operator interpretation when an additional representation is supplied, without attempting a classification of K-theory twists. We also investigate descent of differential-geometric structures and, under restricted-operator hypotheses, Schwinger cocycles and lifting gerbes for loop groups.

papers.title: Blaschke Conjecture and Complex Geometry
papers.abstract: We provide a complex-geometric approach to the Blaschke conjecture, i.e., that a manifold whose injectivity radius equals its diameter is isometric to a compact rank-one symmetric space (CROSS). In particular, we introduce the great quadric fibration, a complex analogue of the great sphere fibration. Requiring its total space to be a complex submanifold simultaneously explains many properties that a Blaschke manifold is expected to possess, including its Clifford structure, Hopf fibration, and diffeomorphism class. Furthermore, the great quadric bundle coincides with the variety of minimal rational tangents (VMRT) of the ambient Fano variety in the standard CROSS cases, and we explain this through a bend-and-break argument in the setting of the Blaschke conjecture under a suitable complexification assumption. Combining this with Hwang-Mok VMRT recognition, we prove the Blaschke conjecture for manifolds admitting an adapted complex structure on their entire tangent bundles.

papers.title: On Lorentzian torse-forming structure manifolds
papers.abstract: In this paper we introduce a class of non-flat Lorentzian manifolds, called Lorentzian torse-forming structure manifolds (briefly, LTFSMs). This class contains Lorentzian concircular structure manifolds (briefly, LCSMs), LSP-Sasakian manifolds, LP-Sasakian manifolds with coefficient $\alpha$, LP-$\alpha$-Sasakian manifolds, LP-Sasakian manifolds, and LP-$\alpha$-Kenmotsu manifolds. The interrelations among these various classes of manifolds are illustrated in Figures 1 and 2. We investigate several geometric properties of LTFSMs. In particular, we show that the expansion scalar, given by the divergence of $\xi$, is nonzero and nonconstant, and that the flow of $\xi$ is irrotational. In an LCSM, the Ricci operator commutes with the structure tensor $\phi$ [12]. However, it is shown that, in an LTFSM, the Ricci operator does not generally commute with $\phi$. If the gradient of the torse-forming scalar $\alpha$ is collinear with the torse-forming vector field $\xi$, then the Ricci operator commutes with $\phi$, and the manifold reduces to an LCSM. It is known that a conformally flat LCSM is quasi-Einstein and hence is a manifold of quasi-constant curvature. We show that a conformally flat LTFSM is a generalized quasi-Einstein manifold in the sense of Chaki [1] and is also a manifold of generalized quasi-constant curvature. Several curvature-related properties of LTFSMs are established, and their sectional curvature is determined. The existence of LTFSMs is demonstrated through several proper nontrivial examples. We also present examples that are simultaneously LCSMs and LTFSMs, examples of LTFMs characterizing twisted cubic spacetimes, and generalized Robertson-Walker (GRW) spacetimes characterizing LCSMs. Finally, we provide examples of LTFSMs in which the vector field $\xi$ is a unit timelike torse-forming vector field but is not concircular; see Examples 5.6--5.8.

papers.title: Calibrations close to $\mathrm{G}_2$-twistor space
papers.abstract: We study natural structures of the kind of $\mathrm{G}_2$ existing on the unit tangent sphere bundle $SM \rightarrow M$ of any oriented Riemannian 4-manifold $M$. Based on the Harvey-Morgan classification of degree 3 calibrations on $\mathbb{R}^7$, we identity those which can be found on $SM$. We also study the Laplacian of the Sasaki metric on 3-forms.

papers.title: Dirichlet eigenvalue asymptotics on conformally compact Einstein manifolds
papers.abstract: We study the first Dirichlet eigenvalues of large geodesic balls and fixed-width boundary layers on conformally compact Einstein manifolds of dimension $n+1.$ For large balls, we determine the exponential rate of convergence when the spectral bottom is less than $\frac{n^2}{4},$ i.e. the bottom of the continuous spectrum. When it equals the bottom of the continuous spectrum, the second coefficient has two possible values, according to whether the continued resolvent is regular or has a pole there. We also give examples with negative Yamabe conformal infinity realizing both threshold alternatives and construct metrics with a Ricci lower bound that have other second coefficients. Under nonnegative Yamabe conformal infinity, we also find the exact second coefficient for the nonlinear $p$-Laplacian on large balls. For layers defined by a geodesic boundary defining function, we compute the first correction and show that its sign characterizes nonnegative Yamabe conformal infinity.

papers.title: Isotropy sets of periodic geodesic flows on three dimensional manifolds
papers.abstract: A classical theorem of Wadsley states that if all geodesics on a Riemannian manifold M are periodic, then they have a common period, and the geodesic flow induces an S^1-action on the unit tangent bundle. Moreover, a conjecture of Berger asserts that this action is free whenever M is simply connected. In this paper, we investigate the Berger conjecture in dimension three by studying the isotropy set of the S^1-action induced by the geodesic flow. Using Morse theory for the energy functional on the free loop space of M, we establish two results in this direction. First, we show that all isotropy groups of the geodesic flow have odd order. Second, we prove that the geodesic flow either acts freely on the unit tangent bundle $T^1M$ or has at least two singular orbit types. This paper serves as preparation for the subsequent paper The Berger conjecture for three-dimensional manifolds, in which the conjecture is proved in dimension three.

papers.title: Mean curvature nonpositivity and rational connectedness
papers.abstract: Let $(X,\omega)$ be a compact Gauduchon manifold and let $E$ be a holomorphic vector bundle on $X$. We establish equivalent conditions for the existence of a Hermitian metric on $E$ with nonpositive mean curvature. For a non-uniruled compact K\"ahler manifold $X$ satisfying $\mu_{\omega_0,\max}(T_X)=0$ for some Gauduchon metric $\omega_0$, we show that the corresponding maximal destabilizing subsheaf of $T_X$ splits off holomorphically and is polystable of slope zero with respect to every Gauduchon metric. Its complement, if nonzero, is HN-negative with respect to every such metric. In particular, a compact K\"ahler manifold is not uniruled if and only if , for every Gauduchon metric $\omega$, its tangent bundle admits a Hermitian metric with nonpositive $\omega$-mean curvature. We also obtain an uniruledness criterion that includes the case where the maximal slope of $T_X$ is zero, and a Mumford-type characterization of rational connectedness. Under HN-nonnegativity of $T_X$ for one Gauduchon metric, rational connectedness, the vanishing of all holomorphic covariant tensors, and the condition $\kappa^+(X)=-\infty$ are equivalent.

papers.title: Curvature, second variation and Jacobi fields in elastic diffeology
papers.abstract: We develop curvature theory on Blohmann's elastic diffeological spaces. We introduce curvature-tensorial connections, whose curvature factors uniquely through $T_3M$, and show that this property holds on finite-dimensional manifolds and is preserved on mapping spaces. Using a plotwise commutator identity and the elasticity axioms, we establish the classical curvature symmetries for curvature-tensorial Levi-Civita connections. We define sectional curvature and a curvature form on the algebraic exterior square, and demonstrate an obstruction to the usual Ricci trace construction: on $C^\infty(S^1,S^2)$, the relevant curvature endomorphism extends boundedly to the $L^2$ completion but is not trace class. We prove the second variation formula, identify the energy Hessian with the index form, and characterize its null space. Under additional hypotheses, we establish existence and uniqueness of Jacobi fields with prescribed initial data. Finally, non-positive sectional curvature excludes conjugate points, while a negative index direction obstructs length minimization.

papers.title: Classification of analytic conformal product structures
papers.abstract: We classify real-analytic conformal product structures on compact simply connected manifolds in all dimensions $n\ge 2$. We prove that in dimension $2$ and $3$ no such structure exists, while in every dimension $n\ge 4$ the two parallel distributions arise from a global product splitting.

papers.title: Scalar--Mean Rigidity for Hyperbolic Balls in Dimensions $2\le n\le 5$
papers.abstract: In this paper, we prove the non-spin hyperbolic scalar--mean rigidity theorem in dimensions $2\leq n\leq5$, resolving the corresponding low-dimensional case of a problem of Gromov. The proof combines the Jang deformation with capillary $\mu$-bubble dimension reduction. We also establish weighted scalar--mean rigidity for Euclidean ball--torus products in total dimension at most seven and show that its hyperbolic analogue fails.

papers.title: Sharp local scalar-curvature rigidity of spherical caps
papers.abstract: Let $B(\delta)\subset\mathbb S^n$ be a geodesic ball with the round metric $\bar{g}$ of sectional curvature one, where $n\geq3$ and $0<\delta<\pi/2$. We prove local scalar-curvature rigidity under preservation of the induced boundary metric and a one-sided lower bound for the boundary mean curvature. More precisely, every sufficiently small $C^{2,\alpha}$ perturbation $g$ of $\bar{g}$ satisfying $R(g)\geq n(n-1)$ and $H(g)\geq(n-1)\cot\delta$ is round up to a diffeomorphism fixing the boundary pointwise. Inspired by the scalar--vector--tensor decomposition used in the study of Yamabe compactness, we establish positivity of the Brendle--Marques quadratic form in the divergence-free gauge for variations preserving the induced boundary metric and satisfying the joint linearized constraints $D R_{\bar{g}}(h)=D H_{\bar{g}}(h)=0$. The hemisphere counterexamples of Brendle--Marques--Neves show that the radius range is sharp.

papers.title: Scalar curvature integrals on geodesic balls
papers.abstract: We study scalar curvature integrals over geodesic balls on complete noncompact manifolds. Under nonnegative Ricci curvature and rotational symmetry, we prove the sharp bound \[ \int_{B_p(r)}S\text{d}\mu_g \le 2n(n-1)\omega_n \bigl(1-v^{1/(n-1)}\bigr)r^{n-2}, \] when $p$ is the rotational origin. Here $\omega_n$ is the volume of the Euclidean unit ball and $v=V_{M^n}$ is the asymptotic volume ratio. In dimension three, with the center at a pole, we obtain a sharp bound \[ \int_{B_p(r)}S\text{d}\mu_g\le16\pi r, \] without any positive volume growth assumption. We also obtain a bound for every asymptotic volume ratio which is sharp for $0\le v\le1/4$. Under nonnegative sectional curvature and $v>0$, we prove the explicit bound at arbitrary centers \[ \int_{B_p(r)}S\text{d}\mu_g\le12\pi(1-v)v^{-3}r. \] If $0\le1-v\le1/100$, we further obtain \[ \int_{B_p(r)}S\text{d}\mu_g\le\bigl[8\pi(1-v)+200\pi(1-v)^2\bigr]r. \] The leading coefficient $8\pi$ is sharp, and a remainder of quadratic order in $1-v$ is necessary.

papers.title: The sharp Chern--Simons--Sobolev inequality and its variants
papers.abstract: We introduce and prove a new conformally invariant Chern--Simons--Sobolev inequality, and classify all optimizers, which are the Hopf map $\pi:\mathbb{S}^{2n+1}\to\mathbb{CP}^n$ composed with a symplectic diffeomorphism of $\mathbb{CP}^n$ and an orientation-preserving conformal transformation of $\mathbb{S}^{2n+1}$. The proof uses the sharp curl-Sobolev inequality and a rigidity argument for its equality case. Motivated by the main result, we also introduce the spherical Radu--Tchrakian--Yang functional, and prove the global minimality of the Hopf map for radii in a neighborhood of $((n!)^2/n)^{1/(4n-4)}$, and characterize all minimizers. We also prove local instability for sufficiently small and sufficiently large radii, with explicit lower bounds for the Morse index.

papers.title: Fixed geodesics of involutions on $3$-spheres
papers.abstract: Let an isometric involution act on a smooth Riemannian $3$-sphere with sectional curvature at least one. We prove that every one-dimensional connected component of its fixed-point set has length at most $2\pi$, and that the bound is sharp. The proof realizes the fixed circle as the link of a complete totally geodesic surface in a positively curved expanding Ricci soliton and applies Bishop--Gromov comparison to its area growth. The analytic input is an equivariant version of Deruelle's smoothing of positively curved cones. We use Gianniotis--Schulze's equivariant local deformation and explain a marked compactness argument for arbitrary finite isotropy. In particular, the end chart retains the specified group action, rather than only an unspecified conjugate.

papers.title: Rigidity theorems of complete self-shrinkers in the Euclidean space
papers.abstract: We classify complete Lagrangian self-shrinking surfaces in $\mathbb{R}^{4}$ with constant squared norm of the mean curvature vector, without assuming an upper bound for the second fundamental form. Their images are a plane through the origin, the round cylinder $S^1(1)\times \mathbb{R}$, or the Clifford torus $S^1(1)\times S^1(1)$. More generally, a complete self-shrinking surface in $\mathbb{R}^{4}$ with constant $|\vec{H}|^2$ is either a plane, a round cylinder, or a complete minimal immersion into $S^3(\sqrt2)$. The proof uses the function $|x|^2-|\vec{H}|^2$, the Bochner formula, and completeness.

papers.title: On complete Ricci--flat K\"ahler manifolds
papers.abstract: We study complete noncompact Ricci-flat K\"ahler manifolds. In the case of Euclidean volume growth, we prove that the underlying complex manifold is naturally quasi-projective and that the asymptotic cone is unique. Moreover, we establish no semistability at infinity and prove convergence to the asymptotic cone at a polynomial rate. In the case of sub-Euclidean volume growth, we construct complete Ricci-flat K\"ahler threefolds with bounded sectional curvature and finite topological type that admit no K\"ahler compactification.

papers.title: Generalized Kahler BHE threefolds
papers.abstract: We study the notion of generalized Kahler Bismut--Hermitian--Einstein (GKBHE) manifolds, namely generalized K\"ahler manifolds for which both Bismut Ricci forms vanish, and we develop a theory for such structures on compact threefolds. We organize the analysis according to the horizontal rank, an invariant taking values in $\{0,1,2\}$ that measures the relative position of the canonical foliations associated with the two Hermitian structures. We characterize the case of horizontal rank $0$ (which corresponds to K\"ahler Ricci flat geometry) and describe the case of horizontal rank $1$, revealing its close interplay with the steady $\nu$-soliton equation in K\"ahler geometry. This description also provides a tool for constructing new compact GKBHE threefolds.

papers.title: Mellin transformed exponential volumes and probabilistic moduli spaces
papers.abstract: A decorated surface is a surface with boundary and a finite set of marked boundary points called cusps. We continue to study the exponential volumes E(S,K,L) of moduli spaces of ideal hyperbolic structures on a decorated surface S, with the given values of lengths of boundary geodesic circles L and boundary geodesic intervals K, introduced in our previous work: 1. We prove that the Mellin--Laplace transform of E(S,K,L) admits Barnes integral presentations, and satisfies recursions, generalising Mirzakhani's recursions. 2. We specify a subset I of the blue boundary intervals, and assign to them any collection of weights. We show that the Mellin transform of the function E(S,K,L) along the variables K at the blue intervals, evaluated at the weights values, calculates weighted exponential volumes of various moduli spaces. If all boundary intervals are blue and all weights are 1/2, we recover Chekhov's volumes of moduli spaces of hyperbolic surfaces with crowns, discretizing the Schwarzian action. We derive recursions for the weighted exponential volumes. 3. We introduce probabilistic Teichmuller spaces related to decorated surfaces S. They are infinite dimensional and carry canonical Wiener type measures. The definition of the measures builds on the works of Bauerschmidt - Losev - Wildemann and Losev. Their quotients by the action of the modular group of S are probabilistic moduli spaces. We show that their volumes are finite. We prove recursion formulas for these measures, and hence for the volumes. The emerging theory generalizes the Schwarzian field theory of Stanford - Witten from the disc to any decorated surfaces, i.e. to open string format. In particular, we get recursions for the Feynman integrals in Schwarzian field theory on decorated surfaces.

papers.title: Harmonic-Einstein maps and critical metrics for eigenvalues of the conformal Laplacian
papers.abstract: We prove that Clarke critical metrics for the ratio of the first two eigenvalues of the conformal Laplacian on a closed manifold with positive Yamabe constant correspond to harmonic--Einstein maps into a sphere. We discuss some rigidity consequences, as well as an extension to the higher-order GJMS operators.

papers.title: Examples of absolutely minimal polyhedral chains in maximum norm spaces
papers.abstract: We construct explicit area-minimizing polyhedral disks in $\R^n$ with the maximum norm for $n=2,3,4$. Their boundaries are polygonal images of the geodesic circle of length $2\pi$, obtained from $n$ distance functions. Piecewise constant calibrations show that these disks minimize mass among Ambrosio--Kirchheim metric currents with the same boundary. The example for $n=4$ gives the lower bound $11\pi^2/20\approx5.42828$ for Gromov's filling area conjecture. For $n>4$, finite linear programs provide further lower bounds.

papers.title: Complex Monge-Amp\`ere equation for positive $(p,p)$-forms on compact K\"ahler manifolds
papers.abstract: A complex Monge-Amp\`ere equation for differential $(p,p)$-forms is introduced on compact K\"ahler manifolds. For any $1 \leq p < n$, we show the existence of smooth solutions unique up to adding constants. For $p=1$, this corresponds to the Calabi-Yau theorem proved by S. T. Yau, and for $p=n-1$, this gives the Monge-Amp\`ere equation for $(n-1)$ plurisubharmonic functions studied by Tosatti-Weinkove. For other $p$ values, this defines a non-linear PDE that falls outside of the general framework of Caffarelli-Nirenberg-Spruck. Further, we define a geometric flow for higher-order forms that extends the K\"ahler-Ricci flow naturally to $(p,p)$-forms. As a consequence of our main theorem, we show that this flow exists in a maximal time interval and can be shown to converge under some assumptions. A modified flow is introduced and the convergence of the associated normalized flow is shown.

papers.title: On electrostatic manifolds with boundary
papers.abstract: Static manifolds with boundary were recently introduced in the context of the problem of prescribing both the scalar curvature of a Riemannian manifold and the mean curvature of its boundary. These manifolds are also of interest from the perspective of general relativity. In this article, we introduce electrostatic manifolds with boundary as a natural generalization of static manifolds with boundary in the presence of a nonzero electric field. We also introduce Robin electrostatic quadruples, extending the notion of Robin static triples previously introduced by the second author. We establish several uniqueness theorems for suitable regions of the Reissner-Nordstr\"om manifold. Finally, we characterize the criticality of the first eigenvalue of an associated mixed Robin-Dirichlet Schr\"odinger operator under admissible volume-preserving variations in terms of the equality of the surface gravities along the Dirichlet boundary components.

papers.title: Non-existence of cohomogeneity one Einstein metrics of two summands
papers.abstract: We prove the non-existence of cohomogeneity one Einstein metrics on a class of compact manifolds arising as double disk bundles, whose principal orbits split into two inequivalent irreducible summands. The proof uses a phase space barrier argument that yields a new obstruction to the existence of closed cohomogeneity one Einstein metrics, even when the principal orbits admit homogeneous Einstein metrics.
